module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Difference of digit sums in base 3 and base 2

Difference of sums of digits of $n$ in ternary and in binary:
$$a(n) = \sum \mathrm{digits}_3(n) - \sum \mathrm{digits}_2(n).$$

*References:*
- [A180017](https://oeis.org/A180017)-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA180017

/-- Difference of sums of digits of $n$ in ternary and in binary. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  (Nat.digits 3 n).sum - (Nat.digits 2 n).sum

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 0 := by norm_num [a]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 0 := by norm_num [a]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 1 := by norm_num [a]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = -1 := by norm_num [a]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 1 := by norm_num [a]

/--
"This sequence is positive on average, since 1/log(3) > 1/log(4). Do all integers appear
infinitely often?" - Charles R Greathouse IV, Feb 07 2013-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (z : ℤ) : Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | a n = z} := by
  sorry

end OeisA180017

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2105.11173 — Lukas Spiegelhofer, Collisions of digit sums in bases 2 and 3, v2; Theorem 1.1, subsequent remarks, and open-problems section
review.notes: Checked all seven declarations and found no mathematical mismatch. OEIS A180017 was read through its data mirror because the main page returned a browser challenge. The definition elaborates to integer subtraction after casting both natural-number digit sums, so negative values are preserved. The empty digit lists at n = 0 correctly give a(0) = 0. Lean checks matched all 10,001 entries of the published table and independently proved the complete 93-term prefix. The conjecture quantifies over every integer z and requires infinitely many natural-number indices with a(n) = z, exactly matching Greathouse's question. A scratch proof also verified equivalence with occurrence above every natural-number bound. The linked Spiegelhofer theorem establishes the z = 0 special case; the consulted sources do not record a resolution of the full universally quantified conjecture, so no status issue is reported. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and compile successfully.
